newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BRAZIL WIN COPA AMERICA THE HARD WAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL WIN COPA AMERICA THE HARD WAY.

text.p: Brazil won the Copa America the hard way on Sunday, surviving a second half bombardment and then scoring twice in the last 15 minutes to beat Bolivia 3-1 in the Sunday.

Brazil striker Ronaldo had looked one of the players least likely to score until the 79th minute, when he put Brazil 2-1 ahead. Ze Roberto then scored in injury time to give Brazil their fifth Copa America title and their first outside their own country.
The two goals came after Brazil, clearly struggling to cope with the difficulties of playing at 3,600 metres above sea level, had been run ragged in the second half.
Edmundo, standing in for the injured Romario, had given Brazil a first half lead but the world champions were on the ropes from the moment that Taffarel relived his La Paz nightmare.

A horrendous misjudgement by the Brazil goalkeeper -- a veteran of two World Cups -- on the stroke of halftime allowed a 35-metre shot by Erwin Sanchez to sneak between him and the post for the Bolivia equaliser.
Four years ago, Taffarel had scored an own goal as Bolivia beat Brazil 2-0 to hand the current world champions their first and only defeat in a World Cup qualifier.
Brazil, clearly hampered by the thin air and cold, were only half the team that had won their five previous games at sea level in Santa Cruz.

Their well-oiled tactical system simply ceased to function, and at times in the second half the Bolivians, who like Brazil had a perfect percent record on their way to the final, appeared to have an extra two or three players on the field.
Bolivia, sensing Taffarel's uneasiness, took pot shots at his goal from outside the penalty after the break.
Brazil were saved by the crossbar twice while several other shots went flying narrowly wide with the beleagured goalkeeper seemingly uncertain as to whether to leave them or not.

But Taffarel also made up for his blunder, making a superb save on the hour to parry away a powerful, close-range drive by Julio Cesar Baldivieso. Shortly afterwards, he dived bravely at the feet of Sanchez to make another important save.
Edmundo had put Brazil in front in the 37th minute from a rebound after Bolivia goalkeeper Carlos Trucco had failed to hold a low, swerving 30-metre kick by Roberto Carlos.
The 45,000 crowd, who had seen their team enjoy the better of the first half, were briefly silenced but came back to life again after Sanchez's equaliser.

A Bolivia goal seemed only a matter of time after the break until Ronaldo, who has been the subject of a tug-of-war between European clubs over his future, latched on to a long through ball by Denilson and scored with a powerful 20-metre drive.
It was the fifth goal of the tournament for Ronaldo, who had barely touched the ball in the second half.
Substitute Ze Roberto finished off a sweet move to score again in injury time, after the Bolivians had clearly lost heart.

Bolivia's players claimed that Edmundo had elbowed Luis Cristaldo in the second half but the Brazil striker was immediately substituted by Paulo Nunes with referee Jorge Nieves seemingly oblvious to the trick that was being played.
Nieves left numerous crude tackles unpunished and never mastered the art of keeping defenders nine metres away at free kicks.

Bolivia - 1-Carlos Trucco, 7-Sergio Castillo, 3-Marco Sandy, 5-Oscar Sanchez, 16-Luis Cristaldo, 6-Vladimir Soria, 10-Marco Etcheverry, 21-Erwin Sanchez, 9-Jaime Moreno (18-Milton Coimbra,74), 10-Marco Etcheverry, 21-Erwin Sanchez
